title: The Mertens function is unbounded on the square-root scale
credit: Classical (Ingham 1942; Odlyzko–te Riele 1985); see Hurst 2018 for status.
premise_risks: Under RH the problem may be as hard as proving linear independence-type statements; difficulty is high
plain: The Mertens function M(x) adds up the Möbius function μ(n) for n ≤ x. Mertens guessed |M(x)| < √x, which was disproved in 1985 without an explicit counterexample, and we now know M(x)/√x exceeds about 1.83 in absolute value infinitely often. Prove that M(x)/√x is unbounded.
math: Let $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)$. Prove $\limsup_{x\to\infty}|M(x)|/\sqrt{x}=+\infty$; i.e. for every $C>0$ there is $x$ with $|M(x)|>C\sqrt x$.
